supersedes_note: The 4 Aug review applied a rubric under which any unenumerated difference was material, so it rejected 27 of 30 pairs on movable clutter — tea towels, toasters, toiletry bottles — while describing genuine fixed-fitting drift as one bullet among many. The owner rejected that reading on 5 Aug 2026: a pair fails when the room stops being the same room, not when a tenant moves a towel. The earlier report is retained unchanged as evidence.

rejects: fixed fabric differs: room geometry, walls, ceilings, floors, finishes, windows, doors
a fitted or fixed unit, appliance, sanitary fitting, radiator or light fitting moves, resizes, changes model or disappears
large fitted or defining furniture is swapped for a different item
the two views of one timepoint contradict each other about any of the above
no enumerated material change is observable, so the pair carries no delta signal
records_but_does_not_reject: movable everyday objects: textiles, toiletries, worktop clutter, small decor, shoes, books
an object of that kind moving, appearing or disappearing
modest camera framing drift that still shows the same part of the room
materiality_rubric.why: The pilot exists to measure compare behaviour on delta pairs. A moved tea towel is a real change a compare run may report, so it belongs in observed gold; it is not evidence that the generator failed to hold the room. An oven that moves is.

room_identity_findings.description: The oven sits lower in the base-unit run at T1. At T0 its control strip meets the underside of the worktop with the hob immediately above it; at T1 there is a clear band of cabinet between worktop and oven top, and the hob has grown and shifted right. Confirmed on a full-resolution crop: the window sill and wall-unit edges hold position, so this is the appliance moving, not the camera.

The T1 frame is not the T0 corner. It is a wider view containing a radiator, a light switch and a window looking onto trees; the T0 frame is a close view of the base units with no radiator and no window in shot.
The T1 D-condition window shows green trees while both A-wide frames show a brick building through the kitchen window, so the two T1 views do not describe the same room.
